exposure: mode of birth (cesarean delivery in the first stage of labor)
cohort: The study included 41 primigravidae (29 with vaginal delivery and 12 with cesarean delivery in the first stage of labor) who underwent MRI scans.
finding: Vaginal delivery, or even active labor itself, may both lead to levator ani (LA) atrophy, but the LA morphology is basically similar in different delivery modes at 10 months postpartum once the onset of labor has occurred.
mod_finding: Significant differences in LA volume (LVOL), levator hiatus length (LH-L), puborectalis attachment width (PAW), levator-symphysis gap (LSG), and levator hiatus width (LH-W) were observed between vaginal delivery and cesarean section groups at 6 weeks postpartum, with LA avulsion and significant 2-D morphological change only observed after vaginal delivery.
